source: Daily Investment Brief Macroeconomic Dashboard + MacroMicro + primary-source cross-checks
sourceStatus: Daily Investment Brief is the primary dashboard, but its live indicator values render client-side and returned placeholders in the machine-readable fetch. Power Stack therefore never interprets 'Analyzing' or '--' as data; missing readings are supplemented with MacroMicro and authoritative source checks.
methodology: Directional channels are scored from -2 to +2. Dashboard data is an input, not an investment signal. Creator/video and social-flow claims are hypothesis generators only and have zero direct scoring weight until independently verified.
regime: Higher real/nominal yields + energy/product inflation + strong physical capex, with fragile breadth beneath the indices

channels.label: Growth / Demand
channels.regime: Resilient headline growth; weaker rate-sensitive breadth
channels.interpretation: Copper and physical capex remain constructive, but small caps, housing and other rate-sensitive areas are weakening. Treat this as uneven late-cycle resilience, not broad acceleration.

channels.label: Policy Relief
channels.interpretation: Oil-driven inflation and hawkish Fed communication have pushed the market toward renewed hike risk rather than easing. Long-duration equities lose a key valuation tailwind.

channels.label: Financial Conditions
channels.regime: Global bond selloff / higher real yields
channels.interpretation: US 10Y is around 4.76–4.78%, 10Y real TIPS about 2.34%, and Japan 10Y reached 3%. Higher discount rates and term premium penalize leverage, speculative duration and capital-intensive projects.

channels.label: Broad Credit
channels.interpretation: Financing is still available to quality issuers, but the cost of capital is rising. Separate access to credit from cheap credit.

channels.label: Weak-End Credit Stress
channels.interpretation: CCC-and-lower yields near 14.6% and higher risk-free rates increase refinancing stress. This is a headwind for levered consumers, speculative AI financing and development-stage equities.

channels.label: Consumer
channels.regime: Selective pressure from fuel and financing costs
channels.interpretation: Higher gasoline/diesel and borrowing costs are a tax on households. Consumer demand has not collapsed, but discretionary and travel exposure deserve a higher hurdle.

channels.label: Housing
channels.interpretation: The long-end yield breakout is directly adverse for mortgages, builders and housing-linked capex. Housing remains one of the clearest places where bond stress transmits to the real economy.

channels.label: Industrial / Power Capex
channels.interpretation: Copper, electrical backlogs, data-centre power demand and continued AI investment support the physical-capex thesis. Higher yields make financing quality and cash conversion more important, not the demand theme irrelevant.

channels.label: Input Costs
channels.interpretation: Oil, diesel/refined products, freight and fertilizer constraints are broadening cost pressure. This favors producers with pricing power and hurts low-margin users of energy/freight.

channels.label: Labour
channels.interpretation: Do not overstate the labor signal before JOLTS and payrolls. Current macro risk is being driven more by energy and bonds than by a confirmed labor break.

channels.label: Risk Appetite
channels.regime: Crowded exposure, narrow index action, active rotation
channels.interpretation: A secondary reproduction puts NAAIM exposure at 102.7, while software/energy/agriculture rotation is happening under flat indices. The claimed record QQQ block trade is not independently verified and receives zero direct score impact.

channels.label: Crude
channels.interpretation: Brent is above $91 and visible Hormuz traffic remains far below normal. Morgan Stanley's $100 Q4 peak forecast is now consistent with a tighter supply path, but high prices can destroy demand and accelerate supply rerouting.

channels.label: Refined Products
channels.interpretation: Diesel/distillate tightness remains a more important inflation channel than crude alone. Refiners and integrated producers benefit more directly than airlines, cruises and freight-intensive consumers.

channels.label: US Gas / Global LNG
channels.regime: US feedgas manageable; global LNG security premium rising
channels.interpretation: Henry Hub near $2.93 keeps US feedgas economics manageable while Gulf/LNG disruption and European storage risk support US export infrastructure such as Cheniere.
